info.name: Courses4Me API v2
info.description: Courses4Me backend v2 (Express + MySQL). Collection variables hold test accounts only — never real customers.

request.description: Always 200; the db field is up|down. Every response carries an X-Request-Id header.

item.name: 1. Authentication (Customer)
item.description: Customer portal signup/login and own-profile endpoints. Login stores {{token}}.

request.description: Creates a customer account. Password: 8+ chars, one uppercase, one number, one symbol.
Customer login. Admin/editor accounts are refused here (use 2. Admin Auth). 5 wrong passwords lock the account for 15 minutes (423 ACCOUNT_LOCKED).
Returns { exists } — true when an account or a past booking uses this email.
Full profile including activityHistory.
Partial update — only sent fields change (name, email, phone, jobTitle, bio, profileImage). profileImage may be a URL or a data:image base64 string.
Bumps tokenVersion, so every existing session (including {{token}}) is logged out — run Login again afterwards. The account owner receives a password-changed email.

item.name: 2. Admin Auth
item.description: Admin panel login and OTP password reset. Login stores {{adminToken}}; Verify OTP stores {{reset_token}}.

request.description: Admin panel login. A login from a new device (user-agent + IP) raises an admin notification. 5 wrong passwords lock the account for 15 minutes (423 ACCOUNT_LOCKED).
Always answers 200 with a generic message. Emails a 6-digit OTP valid for 10 minutes (max 3 emails per account per hour).
Exchange the emailed code (field `code` or `otp`) for a single-use reset token valid 10 minutes.

exec: try { jsonData = pm.response.json(); } catch (error) { throw new Error("Verify OTP response is not valid JSON"); }

request.description: Consumes {{reset_token}}, sets the password and logs every session out.

item.name: 3. Portal Password Reset
item.description: Customer forgot-password via emailed link. The link is FRONTEND_URL/reset-password?token=…; paste the token into {{reset_token}}.

request.description: Always answers 200 with a generic message. Admin accounts are ignored here. Max 3 emails per account per hour.
Legacy body { token, password } is still accepted.

item.name: 4. User Management (Admin)
item.description: Requires {{adminToken}} with role admin (editors are refused).

query.description: active | inactive | suspended | blocked | pending verification

request.description: Users with activityHistory and booking stats (totalBookings, totalSpent, completedCourses, attendanceStatus).
{ counts: { customer, admin, editor, total } }
Suspended/blocked users cannot log in and existing tokens are refused with 403.
Wipes the activity timeline and status reason, leaving one "History Cleared" entry.

item.name: 5. Social Login (browser)
item.description: Redirect flows — open these URLs in a browser, not in Postman. The callback redirects to FRONTEND_URL/<redirect>?token=<jwt>.

item.name: 6. Courses
item.description: Public catalogue and admin course management. Writes need {{adminToken}} with the admin role. Venue postcodes are geocoded server-side, so they must be real UK postcodes that match the venue name.

query.description: SIA Training | Specialist | First Aid | Health & Safety | Hospitality
Published | Draft | Archived (drafts need an admin token)
matches venue name, address or postcode

request.description: Without an admin token only Published courses are returned. Each course carries its lists, venues (with schedules) and a flattened `sessions` array.
Course count per category: [{ _id, count }]. Published only unless an admin token is sent.
A draft or archived course answers 403 without an admin token. An unknown id answers 404.

Required: title, category, duration, shortDescription (20+ chars), fullDescription, pricing.basePrice. Send multipart/form-data with `thumbnail` / `instructorPhoto` files to upload images instead of passing URLs; nested fields then go as JSON strings.
Only the fields sent are changed. Sending `highlights`, `learningPoints`, `targetAudience`, `requirements` or `locations` replaces that list entirely; leaving one out keeps it.
Removes the course with its lists, venues and schedules.

item.name: 7. Locations
item.description: Training venues. Reads are public; writes need {{adminToken}}. Postcodes are stored upper-case.

query.description: matches name, city, postcode or venue name

request.description: Paginated (default 20 per page). `linkedCoursesCount` counts active links to published courses.

exec: if (body.data && body.data[0] && body.data[0].id) { pm.collectionVariables.set("locationId", body.data && body.data[0] && body.data[0].id); }

request.description: Here `linkedCoursesCount` counts every link, whatever its status.
Links of this location, each with a short course summary.
Required: name, addressLine1, city, postcode. Facilities: wifi, projector, whiteboard, catering, toilets, disabled_access, prayer_room, air_conditioning.

body.raw:
{
  "name": "London Centre",
  "venueName": "Westminster Training Rooms",
  "addressLine1": "1 Test Street",
  "addressLine2": "Floor 2",
  "city": "London",
  "postcode": "SW1A 1AA",
  "country": "United Kingdom",
  "mapsUrl": "https://maps.google.com/?q=SW1A+1AA",
  "parking": true,
  "parkingNotes": "Paid street parking outside",
  "accessibility": "Step-free access and a lift to all floors",
  "transport": "5 minutes from Westminster station",
  "facilities": [
    "wifi",
    "projector",
    "toilets",
    "disabled_access"
  ],
  "mainImage": "https://res.cloudinary.com/demo/image/upload/sample.jpg",
  "gallery": [
    "https://res.cloudinary.com/demo/image/upload/sample.jpg"
  ],

  "localVenues": "Stadiums, bars and event spaces across Westminster.",

  "status": "Active"
}

request.description: Only the fields sent change. Sending `facilities` or `gallery` replaces that list; leaving it out keeps it.
Send `{}` to flip the status, or a status to set it. An inactive location cannot be linked to a course.

item.name: 8. Course Scheduling
item.description: A course offered at a location: its price, deposit terms and dated sessions. Seats are reported as availability — `availableSeats` is what is left and `bookedSeats` is always 0.

request.description: Active links of published courses, with the full location, a course summary and the dates. Disabled locations are included so the portal can grey them out — check `locationId.status`.

exec: if (body.data && body.data[0] && body.data[0].id) { pm.collectionVariables.set("courseLocationId", body.data && body.data[0] && body.data[0].id); }

query.description: hides inactive links and disabled locations

request.description: Required: locationId and price. A location can only be linked once per course, and an inactive location is refused. `timingsType: "flexible"` uses `weeklyTimings`; "same" uses startTime/endTime.

exec: if (body.data && body.data.dates && body.data.dates[0] && body.data.dates[0].id) { pm.collectionVariables.set("courseLocationDateId", body.data && body.data.dates && body.data.dates[0] && body.data.dates[0].id); }

request.description: When `dates` is sent it is the complete set: entries with an `_id` are updated, new entries are added and anything missing is deleted. Omit `dates` to leave the schedule untouched.
Returns the date with `seatsRemaining` and `availabilityStatus` (Available / Selling Fast / Sold Out).
Removes the link and every date under it.

item.name: 9. Bookings
item.description: Checkout, lookups and the admin booking actions. A booking holds its seat for 60 minutes; after that the expiry job cancels it and puts the seat back on sale.

request.description: Public. Takes a seat on the chosen session, creates the customer account when the email is new, and returns a PENDING booking. The price comes from the course-location link, not from the payload. A second active booking of the same course is refused, and a full session answers 400.
Public — the booking-success page uses it. A pending booking is re-checked against Stripe first, in case the webhook was delayed.

item.name: My Booking Status for a Course

request.description: Returns PAID / PENDING / NONE plus the sessions this student already holds.
Groups the student's bookings into upcoming / ongoing / completed / postponed / cancelled with summary stats.

query.description: Confirmed | Pending | Cancelled | Expired | All Booking Status
Pending | Paid | Failed | Refunded | Refund Requested | All Payments
name, email, booking id or course title

request.description: One row per customer and course: a paid booking hides an older pending one for the same course.
status: PENDING | PAID | EXPIRED | CANCELLED. paymentStatus: Pending | Paid | Failed | Refunded.
Actions: extend, reschedule, postpone, cancel, complete, resume. Each one is recorded on the customer's activity timeline and emails the student.

Within 48 hours of the course, or without `forceBypass48h`, the student is sent a £70 payment link and the new dates wait in `pendingReschedule` until the fee is paid. Maximum two reschedules, and only within six months of the original date.
Applies the new dates immediately, with no fee.
Only the booking owner, only a PAID booking, and only while the course is still upcoming. Send as multipart/form-data with a `proof` file to attach evidence.

approve or reject. Approving refunds at Stripe, cancels the booking, puts the seat back on sale and emails the student. `refundType: "partial"` refunds the total minus `deductionAmount`. Admin or editor.

item.name: 10. Customers (Admin)
item.description: The customers table of the admin panel, served from the bookings module.

request.description: Each customer carries `bookingCount` and `totalSpent` (paid bookings only).
Includes the customer's bookings and what they have spent.
Removes the account and its bookings.

item.name: 11. Payments (Stripe)
item.description: Stripe checkout and the webhook. Set STRIPE_SECRET_KEY and STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET in .env; without them these endpoints answer 503.

request.description: Returns the hosted Stripe page URL for the booking. Expired or cancelled bookings are refused.
For the embedded card form: returns `clientSecret`. A booking that is already paid answers 400.

Handles checkout.session.completed, payment_intent.succeeded and payment_intent.payment_failed. The signature is verified against STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, so a hand-made request answers 400. A payment arriving after the booking expired is re-seated when a seat is free, or refunded automatically when not.

item.name: 12. Dashboard & Analytics
item.description: The admin home and analytics pages. Both are admin only — they carry revenue figures.

request.description: Returns `stats` (course totals, bookings and revenue for the range), `performanceData` and `categoryData` for the charts, `recentActivity`, the latest `bookings`, `lowSeats` (sessions with 5 seats or fewer, from both scheduling systems) and `pendingApprovals` (draft courses).
Six months of new against returning customers, six months of paid revenue, and the five courses earning the most with their share of total revenue.

item.name: 13. Notifications
item.description: The bell menu. Notifications are written for admins and editors when an alert category is enabled in Settings; each user only ever sees their own.

request.description: The 20 most recent, newest first, with `unreadCount`.
Answers 401 for a notification belonging to someone else.

item.name: 14. Settings
item.description: Platform settings. The row is created with the defaults the first time it is read. The `notifications` toggles decide which alerts are written, and `emailTemplates[].isActive` decides which customer emails are sent.

request.description: Only the blocks you send are replaced, so this leaves the toggles and templates untouched.
Switching a category off stops that alert being written for the admins.
Sending this array replaces the whole list. `isActive: false` stops that email being sent; an unknown key is treated as active so mail is never switched off by accident.

item.name: 15. Licences
item.description: The SIA-style credentials sold alongside the courses. Reads are public; writes need {{adminToken}}. A licence carries its own venues and dated sessions, so it can be booked through `9. Bookings` exactly like a course — post the licence id as `courseId` and one of its schedule ids as `session.scheduleId`.

query.description: SIA Training | First Aid | Health & Safety | Specialist
Published | Draft | Archived (drafts need an admin token)
matches title, licence number, holder name or type

request.description: Paginated (10 per page). The same list comes back under `data` and `licenses`, with `total`, `page` and `limit`. Without an admin token only Published licences are returned.
The licence is returned under `data` and also spread at the top level. Here `relatedCourses` carries the full course records rather than just their ids. A draft answers 403 without an admin token.

Required: title, category, shortDescription, fullDescription, pricing.basePrice. The licence number, holder id and a three-year expiry are generated, and `holderName` defaults to the title. `pricingBreakdown[].price` is free text so it prints as written ("£220", "Included").

Only the fields sent change. Sending `highlights`, `learningPoints`, `requirements`, `applicationSteps`, `pricingBreakdown`, `relatedCourses` or `locations` replaces that block entirely; leaving one out keeps it.
Removes the licence with its lists, steps, fee table, course links, venues and sessions.
The booking endpoint takes a licence id just as it takes a course id: the booking comes back with `courseModel: "License"` and holds a seat on the licence session.
